data.title: AXT in focus as Wedbush weighs in on potential China delays
data.description:
• Amid a report that China is delaying the passage of certain critical materials such as germanium, quartz, and neodymium, it hasn't yet impacted semiconductor materials companies, Wedbush Securities said.
  • “China's role as a key supplier of critical materials and the Chinese government's willingness to moderate or halt supply remain points to watch given key elements (like rare earths or indium) are often core building blocks required for data center necessities (motors, optics, etc.), with past shortages of neodymium for instance having weighed heavily on the HDD industry,” Wedbush Securities analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to clients. “Having said this, it has appeared lately that China's reluctance to ship product freely hasn't risen to the level of extremely disruptive for most of our coverage (ex. AXTI), and rather proven to be a potential stumbling block that requires management.”
  • AXT is one of the larger manufacturers of indium phosphide, gallium arsenide, and germanium, all of which have many uses, including in semiconductors.

data.title: Docebo raises buyback price to $25/share, extends offer deadline
data.description:
• Docebo (DCBO) has raised the price of its previously announced $70M share buyback to $25 per share, up from $20.40, and extended the offer deadline to Sept. 8, 2026.
  • The higher price reduces the maximum number of shares the company can repurchase to 2.8M, compared to 3.4M shares previously. All other terms remain unchanged.

data.title: Arbutus to repurchase up to $230M of shares in tender offer
data.description:
• Arbutus Biopharma (ABUS) said it plans to launch a modified Dutch auction tender offer to repurchase up to $230M of its common shares at $5 to $5.75 per share.
  • The offer is expected to begin on or around Aug. 24 and expire around Sept. 29, with the company using cash on hand to fund the repurchases.
  • Stock up 12% in Friday premarket trading.

data.title: Marvell's deal with Google indicates that custom silicon is 'advantageous,' Wedbush says
data.description:
Marvell Technology's (MRVL) announcement this week that it is working with Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) to develop custom AI chips is indicative that custom silicon is “advantageous,” Wedbush Securities said.

“Net, we don't see this outcome as necessarily unexpected,” Wedbush Securities analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to clients. “More importantly, we believe this spate of news and speculation reiterates that in the current environment, companies with custom silicon design capabilities as well as IP blocks are in an advantageous position and that given the spate of opportunities, it's not necessarily a zero-sum game (e.g., if Marvell owns, AVGO (Google's largest TPU partner) or AMD, or NVDA are necessarily losers).” 

Marvell entered into an expanded partnership on July 29 related to Google's custom semiconductor products. “The expanded partnership spans a comprehensive range of custom silicon programs that attach to the TPU ecosystem, including AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, network interface controllers, memory interface controllers, and near-memory compute,” Marvell said in a filing.

As part of the deal, Marvell issued Google a warrant on Aug. 18 to purchase up to 58.97M shares at an exercise price of $206.58 per share.

Separately, Bryson opined this week on a potential deal between AMD (AMD) and Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) for work on a future TPU, noting such a partnership could be “significant.”

data.title: Qnity appoints semiconductor finance veteran Ken Rizvi as CFO
data.description:
• Qnity Electronics (Q) appointed semiconductor finance veteran Ken Rizvi as senior vice president and chief financial officer, effective October 1.
  • He will succeed Michael Goss, who has served as interim CFO. While, Goss will become Qnity’s vice president of finance and controllership.
  • Ken brings more than 25 years of financial experience, including extensive CFO and senior finance roles across the semiconductor ecosystem. He most recently served as CFO of Synaptics (SYNA), where he oversaw global finance, corporate development, investor relations and IT.

data.title: Wynn Resorts faces a potential employee strike at its Boston property
data.description:
Wynn Resorts' (WYNN) Encore Boston Harbor casino and hotel property in Everett, Massachusetts, is facing the prospect of a labor strike. More than 1,300 unionized workers voted this week to authorize a strike as negotiations over a new labor agreement stalled ahead of the August 31 expiration of their current contract.

The workforce includes hotel and food-service employees such as housekeepers, cooks, servers, bartenders, cleaners, dishwashers, drivers, cocktail servers, bar porters, and slot attendants. The workers are represented primarily by the Unite Here Local 26 and Teamsters Local 25 unions.

Workers want a new contract that improves compensation and protects benefits. Union priorities include a $10 wage increase over four years, continued benefits, and pension protections for longer-serving employees. Union leaders have argued that Encore Boston Harbor has the financial capacity to meet those demands, pointing to approximately $847M in revenue at the resort last year. 

The strike authorization vote does not itself create a strike or set a guaranteed walkout date. However, it permits the union membership and leadership to call one if negotiations fail. If Wynn Resorts and the unions do not reach a settlement or agree to extend the existing agreement, a strike could begin as soon as August 31.

data.title: BJ's Wholesale gains after comparable sales and membership fee income shine in Q2
data.description:
BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings (BJ) gained in early action on Friday after the warehouse club chain released a strong second-quarter earnings report.

Total comparable club sales shot up 11.9% during the quarter. Excluding the impact of gasoline sales, comparable club sales were up 3.1%. Top-line revenue of $6.23B beat the consensus estimate by $290M.

Membership fee income increased 9.9% year-over-year to $135.6M in the second quarter. The increase was primarily driven by strength in membership acquisition, retention, and higher-tier membership penetration across both new and existing clubs. On a smaller scale, the membership fee income growth was stronger than the recent paces for Costco (COST) and Sam's Club (WMT).

The merchandise gross margin rate, which excludes gasoline sales and membership fee income, decreased by approximately 20 basis points compared to a year ago, primarily driven by the company’s continued investments in pricing, partially offset by tariff refund benefits recognized

Adjusted EBITDA increased by 14.3% to $347.2M. Non-GAAP EPS was reported at $1.36 vs. $1.17 consensus and $1.14 a year ago.

"We delivered a strong second quarter, coming in ahead of our expectations across sales and profitability, with strong membership momentum. Our value proposition continued to resonate with members in our clubs and at our gas stations, and the momentum we're seeing across our strategic priorities gives us real confidence in the road ahead," stated CEO Bob Eddy.

Looking ahead, BJ's (BJ) sees comparable club sales, excluding the impact of gasoline sales, increasing 2.0% to 3.0% year-over-year for the full year. Adjusted EPS is seen landing in a range from $4.60 to $4.80 (midpoint $4.70) vs. the consensus estimate of $4.53.

Shares of BJ's (BJ) rose 1.2% in premarket trading to $92.36 vs. the 52-week range of $83.21 to $105.78.
